chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you of the true jurisprudent (faqih)? The true jurisprudent is one who does not cause the people to despair of God's mercy, does not make them feel secure from God's punishment, does not grant them license to commit acts of disobedience to God, and does not abandon the Quran out of a desire for something other than it.'

Indeed, there is no goodness in knowledge that has no understanding in it. Indeed, there is no goodness in recitation that has no reflection in it. Indeed, there is no goodness in worship that has no contemplation in it.

And in another narration (he said): 'Indeed, there is no goodness in knowledge without understanding. Indeed, there is no goodness in recitation without reflection. Indeed, there is no goodness in worship without jurisprudential understanding. Indeed, there is no goodness in a ritual without piety in it.'

key_terms.الفقيه: The jurisprudent (faqih) — one qualified in Islamic law; here redefined beyond legalism to encompass spiritual and pastoral qualities
key_terms.تدبّر: Pondering/reflection — the Quranic act of deliberate contemplation of meaning (cf. Q38:29, Q47:24)
key_terms.تفكّر: Contemplation — inner reflection and thought in worship
key_terms.تفهّم: Deep understanding/comprehension — active engagement with meaning, not mere memorization
key_terms.وَرَع: Piety/scrupulousness — the quality of conscientious restraint from sin, distinguishing genuine devotion from outward ritual

ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of a true Islamic scholar (faqih) according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), the Commander of the Faithful, defines the truly qualified Islamic jurisprudent through four balanced qualities: balancing hope in God's mercy with fear of His punishment, forbidding sinful license-granting, and remaining anchored to the Quran. The Imam then expands this vision with parallel aphorisms insisting that knowledge, Quranic recitation, and worship must each be accompanied by active engagement — understanding (tafahhum), reflection (tadabbur), contemplation (tafakkur), and piety (wara') — or they are spiritually empty. This teaching was directed to Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) companions in a context where pseudo-scholars were either frightening people with excessive warnings or offering false assurances, making this a pointed critique of superficial religious authority.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Abu Saeed Al Qammat, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you all with the understanding one who is truly an understanding one? (It is) the one who does not despair the people from the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and does not liberate them from the Punishment of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and does not permit for them to be in the disobedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and does not neglect the Quran, turning away from it to something else.

Indeed! There is no goodness in a knowledge wherein there is no understanding. Indeed! There is no goodness in the recitation (of the Quran) wherein there is no pondering. Indeed! There is no goodness in a worship there being no thinking in it’.

And in another report, (He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said): ‘Indeed! There is no goodness in a knowledge wherein there is no understanding. Indeed! There is no goodness in a recitation (of the Quran) wherein there is no pondering. Indeed! There is no goodness in a worship there being no thinking in it. There is no goodness in a ritual, there being no piety in it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from ’Isma’il ibn Mihran from abu Sa‘id al-Qammat from al-Halabi from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “Imam Ali (a.s.) said, ‘Do you want me to describe to you the true Faqih, person who truly has a good understanding of religion? A true Faqih is one who does not cause people to despair from the mercy of Allah and does not make them to be unconcerned about the punishment of Allah, who does not allow them to consider disobedience to Allah as permissible and who doe not abandon the holy Quran because of being attracted towards other matters.

You must know that there is no goodness in knowledge without good understand (Fiqh). You must know that there is nothing good in a recitation without thinking about it. You must know that there is nothing good in worship without thoughtfulness.

In another Hadith it says, “ You must know that there is nothing good in a knowledge without good understanding. You must know that there is nothing good in a recitation without thinking about it. You must know that there is nothing good in worship without having a good understanding of religion. You must know that there is nothing good in performing the acts of Hajj etc. without piety.’”
